goal: Implement the first non-default real profile import and exec CLI composition for verified agy 1.1.2 Linux SSH.
completed: Merged the two-account validation evidence in PR 29.
Added hidden compile-time-gated import and real exec commands for the verified agy 1.1.2 Linux contract.
Import extracts only the refresh credential from a secure official home and materializes a minimal managed envelope.
Execution uses direct argv, isolated HOME/XDG runtime, exclusive profile locking, and propagates the child exit code.
Opened PR 30 after the complete local gate passed with 62 automated tests.
nextActions: Review and merge https://github.com/ensp1re/agy-auth/pull/30, then perform a controlled two-profile integration using the installed agy 1.1.2 client.
decisions: Direct refresh-token injection is a viable agy 1.1.2 Linux SSH profile mechanism; the official client continues to own refresh and backend requests.
Real operator-controlled state may be inspected temporarily during authorized research, but independent OAuth enrollment remains gated by product-scope and ADR approval.
openQuestions: Does Google rotate the refresh token during long-lived use, and can agy-auth capture that update atomically per profile?
What at-rest protection should project-owned refresh credentials use?

notRun: Controlled real two-profile CLI integration, rollback journal under injected faults, and client versions beyond 1.1.2 were not run.

risks: The contract is reverse engineered and version-specific; refresh credentials are bearer secrets and require protected storage.
doNotRepeat: Do not copy live access tokens; the minimal refresh-token envelope is sufficient.
Do not enable production switching from single-account evidence.
